question.prompt: The graph of the function \(f(x)=2x^3-7\) goes:

solutions.explanation:
Cubing preserves the sign of \(x\), and the magnitude of \(x^3\) grows without bound as the magnitude of \(x\) grows. Consequently, \(2x^3\) becomes arbitrarily large to the right and arbitrarily negative to the left. Subtracting the fixed number \(7\) shifts the graph down without changing these tail directions.

Therefore the graph goes up to the right and down to the left, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
